Running `habeas add-input` for that record refreshes its required definition input and leaves determination false pending review. {cite}`requirements.definitions.inputs` {cite}`requirements.definitions.capture`
rationale:
The example is covered by one `{test}` reference, at `tests/definitions.rs:51`. It is on `cyclic_dependencies_are_captured_once_and_changes_require_review`. I read the test and its helpers; I did not run it or read the implementation behind it.

Scenario steps and where the test covers them:
- **Starting record.** `fixture()` creates `rules.ready` depending on `glossary.a`, with `a` and `b` forming a cycle. `capture()` calls `add_input` to create the record. `approve()` sets `determination` to true and adds a rationale. The test checks that the record has 3 inputs (the requirement plus the two definitions) and that `validate_repository` reports no errors. That is an approved record with current definition inputs.
- **Definition change.** The test rewrites `md/glossary.md` twice. One edit changes the phrase option (`:phrase: beta` becomes `:phrase: new beta`). The other changes the body text (`See` becomes `Read`).
- **Validation reports stale evidence without modifying the record.** After each edit, `validate_repository` must return an error containing "input text changed" and naming a `glossary.` definition. The test then asserts that the record file's bytes still equal `before`, so the record was not modified.
- **Running `add-input` refreshes the definition input and leaves determination false.** After the edits, `capture(root)` runs `add_input` again. The test asserts `determination == false` and that the inputs still number exactly 3, so there are no duplicates. It then calls `approve`, and `validate_repository` returns no errors. That only holds if the stored definition snapshot was refreshed to the current text.

The same test also checks two neighbouring behaviours. A blank-line move of the definitions causes no invalidation, which supports the `inputs` requirement. An unchanged re-capture leaves the file byte-identical, which supports `capture`.

The setup and assertions cover every step and outcome of the example, so I judge it satisfied.

text: An evidence record has determination true and a current definition input. After the definition changes, validation reports stale evidence without modifying the record. Running `habeas add-input` for that record refreshes its required definition input and leaves determination false pending review. {cite}`requirements.definitions.inputs` {cite}`requirements.definitions.capture`

Evidence inputs MAY have a definition form containing exactly `definition` and `text`. `definition` MUST identify one named definition; `text` MUST contain its complete raw fenced declaration as source lines, including its phrase option and explanatory body.

Validation MUST reject missing definitions and changed snapshot text, identifying the definition and showing a compact diff when available. Moving an unchanged definition within its chapter MUST NOT invalidate its snapshot. Evidence displays MUST show the definition name, current source location, and recorded text.

When `habeas add-input` creates or refreshes evidence, it MUST also capture or refresh the definition inputs required by the resulting record, including dependencies of its subject text and all reviewed inputs.

Repeated references MUST NOT create duplicate definition inputs. Any change to the record MUST leave its determination false pending reassessment. If no inputs or other record contents change, the record MUST remain unchanged.
